## Abstract

Genomic prediction of *Helicobacter pylori* antimicrobial resistance commonly relies on 23S rRNA and *gyrA* mutations, but strong internal accuracy does not establish transportability across studies, sequence products, lineages, and susceptibility-testing methods. We performed an analysis-locked, public-data-only benchmark of frozen clarithromycin and levofloxacin mutation catalogues. A 414-isolate international catalogue cohort was evaluated internally and compared with two Chinese external cohorts: 60 isolates with exact minimum inhibitory concentration and assembly linkage, and 52 isolates with paired reads and study-defined disk-diffusion phenotypes. Deterministic panels were applied without refitting, and a four-domain audit assessed analytic availability, genomic population shift, conditional genotype-phenotype transport, and clinical error severity. Of 526 materialized genomes, 517 passed frozen quality gates. The read cohort supported good but imperfect performance for clarithromycin (90.0% sensitivity; 95.8% specificity) and levofloxacin (87.5%; 95.7%). In the assembly-only cohort, only 6/60 genomes were 23S-callable; varying the alignment task, identity threshold from 70 to 98%, and aligned-query coverage from 0 to 90% recovered no additional final-quality-control target-spanning assembly. Levofloxacin sensitivity in that cohort was 42.9% (95% confidence interval 24.5-62.8), specificity was 75.9% (56.5-89.7), and the false-susceptible rate was 57.1%. Two independent sequence callers agreed for all 57 final-quality-control assemblies, whereas independently recalled and source-reported genotype categories agreed for only 31/57. The performance loss persisted within the dominant single-nucleotide-polymorphism cluster and after lineage standardization; 11/16 missed resistant isolates had a lower-bound minimum inhibitory concentration of at least 8 mg/L. Phenotype-blind rejection based on fixed development-distance percentiles did not rescue Ningxia levofloxacin performance: the lowest eligible false-susceptible rate was 50.0%, and sensitivity was 44.6 percentage points lower than in the read cohort (P=0.0046). These results show that resistance-genotyping transportability must be evaluated as a chain spanning target availability, population shift, conditional genotype-phenotype stability, and clinically directional error.

**Keywords:** *Helicobacter pylori*; antimicrobial resistance; whole-genome sequencing; external validation; population structure; reproducibility

## Impact Statement

Genomic antimicrobial-susceptibility prediction is useful only when sequence data, phenotypes, and mutation rules remain reliable outside the dataset in which a rule was developed. We applied fixed, biologically interpretable 23S rRNA and *gyrA* catalogues to two independently generated Chinese cohorts after auditing genome quality, target callability, relatedness, and population structure. A read-based cohort supported good but imperfect performance. In contrast, an assembly-only cohort was largely uncallable for clarithromycin and showed a high false-susceptible rate for levofloxacin. Independent sequence callers reproduced the deposited *gyrA* calls, but these calls frequently differed from the source-reported genotype categories. The work provides a reusable audit framework for genomic prediction studies and shows why missing targets cannot be treated as wild type. It also demonstrates that isolate-level, version-matched sequence provenance is part of diagnostic validation rather than an administrative detail.

## Data Summary

This study reused public *H. pylori* sequences and isolate-level antimicrobial-susceptibility phenotypes from the HpGP cohort (NCBI BioProject PRJNA529500; https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/bioproject/PRJNA529500), the Ningxia cohort (NCBI BioProject PRJNA745492; https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/bioproject/PRJNA745492), and a paired-read Chinese cohort (Zenodo record 10369064; https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.10369064). Reference sequences were *H. pylori* 26695 (NC_000915.1) and 23S rRNA record U27270.1. Individual sequence identifiers, phenotype links, acquisition checksums, quality-control outcomes, derived predictions, and post-freeze coverage/selective-use stress outputs for all 526 materialized genomes are provided in Supplementary Data S1-S20. The frozen configuration, executable workflows, software environments, tests, compact derived data, and source data for all figures are prepared for public archival release at **[permanent repository URL and version DOI required before submission]**. No new sequence data were generated in this study.

## Introduction

Resistance-guided treatment is increasingly important for *Helicobacter pylori*, yet culture-based susceptibility testing is technically demanding and is not uniformly available. Mutations in 23S rRNA and the quinolone-resistance-determining region of *gyrA* provide biologically interpretable genomic signals for clarithromycin and fluoroquinolone resistance, respectively [@Versalovic1996Clarithromycin; @Cattoir2007Fluoroquinolone; @Binh2014Clarithromycin; @Lauener2019Prediction; @Lyu2023NovelMutations; @Zhou2022Ningxia; @MartinezMartinez2026HpGP]. Their existence is not the unresolved question. The clinically relevant uncertainty is whether a fixed published catalogue retains sensitivity—particularly a low false-susceptible rate—when transported to genuinely independent studies, populations, sequence products, and susceptibility-testing procedures.

Many bacterial genomic-prediction studies use random isolate splits. Such splits can distribute closely related organisms, study-specific laboratory signals, or lineage-associated alleles across training and test sets, creating an optimistic estimate of generalization. This risk is especially relevant in *H. pylori*, whose recombining population structure reflects long-term association with human populations and substantial geographic differentiation [@Falush2022Genetics; @Thorell2023HpGPStructure; @Jin2025Linqu; @Wang2025EasternChina]. A transportability benchmark must therefore distinguish random-split interpolation from independent-study and held-out-lineage performance.

Prior genotype-to-phenotype studies have reported both strong agreement for selected drug–marker pairs and incomplete characterization across broader resistance mechanisms, populations, and sequence products [@Saranathan2020Bronx; @CamorlingaPonce2021Mexico; @DomanovichAsor2020Agreement; @Vieni2025IncompleteAMR; @Wang2025InterpretableML]. Public validation also introduces a more basic reproducibility question: whether an independently recalled genotype from the currently deposited sequence material matches the genotype category reported with the phenotype. A clinically relevant benchmark should not silently substitute source-reported genotypes when deposited sequences are uncallable or discordant.

We therefore evaluated frozen clarithromycin and levofloxacin mutation catalogues without test-cohort marker selection. The design integrated isolate-level data-lineage auditing, raw-read and assembly callability, complete genome-quality control, near-clone grouping, development-only population-cluster fitting, external validation, MIC-aware sensitivity analyses, and phenotype-blind negative controls. The objective was a reproducible boundary assessment: which susceptibility inferences transported, where they failed, and whether apparent performance depended on validation design, lineage, or the reproducibility of the public sequence snapshot.

**Table 1. Four-domain audit-first transportability framework and observed boundary.**

| Domain | Diagnostic question | Primary evidence | Observed boundary |
|---|---|---|---|
| Analytic availability | Can the resistance locus be called from the submitted sequence product? | Frozen genome QC, target-spanning calls, read/assembly concordance, 23S recovery grid | Ningxia 23S was callable in 6/60 assemblies; threshold and task relaxation rescued no additional final-QC sample. |
| Genomic population shift | Is the external cohort exchangeable with the catalogue cohort in phenotype-blind genomic space? | Fixed core-SNP clusters, development-manifold distance, cohort discriminators | External genomes were locally supported but study identity remained learnable (out-of-fold AUC 0.899–0.918). |
| Conditional transport | Does the marker–phenotype relation persist within shared genomic strata? | Within-cluster estimates, lineage standardization, independent callers, residual *gyrA* scan | The Ningxia levofloxacin gap persisted in cluster 3 and after standardization; catalogue expansion explained only 1/16 misses. |
| Clinical consequence | Are errors clinically directional and severe? | False-susceptible gate, MIC lower bounds, bootstrap and leave-one-out analyses | False-susceptible rate was 57.1%; 11/16 missed resistant isolates had lower-bound MIC at least 8 mg/L. |

## Methods

### Study design and analysis lock

This was a retrospective computational validation study using only public genomes and public isolate-level antimicrobial susceptibility phenotypes. Phase 0 was restricted to novelty, linkage, phenotype, breakpoint, overlap, lineage-feasibility, and small technical audits. The decision `CONDITIONAL_GO_CLR_LVX_BINARY` and the complete analysis plan were committed before full-cohort performance was inspected. This internal analysis lock was not a public prospective registration. Subsequent execution corrections were prospectively logged and were not permitted to change cohorts, phenotypes, marker panels, validation gates, or estimands.

### Generative AI assistance

OpenAI Codex (accessed 30-31 August 2026) was used under author direction to assist with code scaffolding, test generation, documentation, consistency checks, and manuscript organization. The authors specified the scientific questions and frozen analysis rules, verified source data and references, reviewed the executable workflows and outputs, and retained responsibility for all interpretations and conclusions. The tool was not used to generate or alter scientific data or to make autonomous clinical or causal claims.

### Cohorts and phenotype authority

HpGP was the catalogue/internal cohort [@Thorell2023HpGPStructure; @MartinezMartinez2026HpGP]. Of 419 phenotype identifiers, 414 had exact current assembly-name links and were retained. The primary external cohort comprised 60 Ningxia isolates with exact assembly linkage and isolate-level MICs measured by Etest [@Zhou2022Ningxia]. The secondary external method-stress cohort comprised 52 isolates with exact paired-read and categorical phenotype linkage [@Yu2023ZenodoCohort]; its study-defined disk-diffusion labels, including overlapping levofloxacin zone endpoints, were retained without breakpoint optimization. Each cohort was reported separately. Both external cohorts were Chinese, precluding a claim of global external validation.

Published phenotype labels were the primary authority. Exact MIC strings, inequality operators, assay method, medium, incubation metadata, breakpoint source, recomputed interpretation, and a prespecified borderline-MIC flag were retained when available. Primary binary analyses excluded intermediate or ambiguous labels. Sensitivity analyses used recomputed labels, intermediate-as-susceptible and intermediate-as-resistant interpretations, and exclusion of borderline MICs.

### Frozen genomic panels

The clarithromycin panel classified resistance when 23S rRNA A2142G, A2142C, or A2143G was detected. The levofloxacin panel classified resistance when *gyrA* A88V, A88P, N87K, N87I, D91G, D91N, or D91Y was detected. Common 23S labels were reconciled to U27270.1 feature coordinates before cohort-wide calling. No external phenotype was used to add, remove, or reprioritize variants.

### Sequence processing and genome quality

All public inputs were acquired with expected-byte, repository-MD5, archive-integrity, and local-SHA-256 checks. Assemblies were screened using the frozen 1.4–1.9 Mb genome-size interval and maximum 300 contigs, followed by CheckM2 completeness at least 90% and contamination at most 10% [@Chklovski2023CheckM2]. Failed genomes remained in attrition outputs but could not define relatedness groups, core-SNP clusters, or diagnostic denominators.

For assemblies, standardized megablast target alignments required at least 90% identity. A 23S call additionally required at least 5% aligned-query coverage and explicit mapping of both U27270.1 feature positions 2143 and 2144; *gyrA* required at least 90% aligned-query coverage. Target absence or assembly breakage was uncallable, not wild type. A post-freeze sensitivity grid varied BLAST task, identity threshold from 70% to 98%, and aligned-query coverage from 0% to 90% while retaining the requirement that both 23S marker bases were spanned. For the read cohort, fastp-cleaned paired reads were mapped to *H. pylori* 26695 and to a pooled 23S reference. Calls required depth at least 10, mapping and base quality at least 20, and major-allele fraction at least 0.80. A pooled resistant 23S fraction at least 0.20 produced a resistant call; copy-specific mappings were retained as an audit. All three bases of *gyrA* residues 87, 88, and 91 had to be callable. SKESA support assemblies [@Souvorov2018SKESA] entered genome QC and population analyses, but raw-read panel predictions remained authoritative.

### Relatedness and phenotype-blind population structure

Exact isolate, sample, run, and assembly overlaps were audited before validation. A near-clone edge required Mash distance at most 0.001 [@Ondov2016Mash], skani average nucleotide identity at least 99.9% [@Shaw2023Skani], and aligned fraction at least 0.90 in both directions. Connected components were the grouping unit for clone-aware cross-validation and bootstrap resampling.

Snippy 4.6.0 generated SNP-only calls against strain 26695 using mapping/base quality 20, VCF quality 20, and minimum depth 10. Non-SNP FreeBayes observations were excluded. Sparse site-by-alternate-allele features were selected using HpGP sequences only. A 20-component truncated singular-value decomposition and eight-cluster K-means solution were fitted only in HpGP; external genomes were transformed and assigned to fixed centroids without refitting. These de novo clusters served as leakage groups and were not interpreted as formal named *H. pylori* populations.

For a continuous measure of proximity to the development population, the first 10 development-fitted component scores were standardized using HpGP means and standard deviations. Each genome's distance was defined as the mean Euclidean distance to its five nearest HpGP genomes, excluding self-neighbours for HpGP. Cohort lineage-composition shift was summarized by Jensen–Shannon distance between projected cluster-frequency distributions. Within each external drug analysis, distances were compared between correct and incorrect calls by Mann–Whitney tests and Cliff's delta. These distances were descriptive measures of geometric support, not calibrated out-of-distribution probabilities.

### External validation and leakage benchmark

Deterministic panels were applied without refitting. Prespecified L2 logistic regression (`C=1`, liblinear, threshold 0.5) compared mutation-only, lineage-only, and mutation-plus-lineage features. Validation included 100 stratified 80:20 random-isolate splits, five-fold near-clone-grouped validation, eligible leave-country-out and leave-lineage-out folds, and direct HpGP-to-external tests. Held-out groups required at least 30 isolates, including at least 10 susceptible and 10 resistant outcomes.

### Source-genotype and independent-caller audit

For the Ningxia cohort, source-reported per-isolate genotype categories were transcribed independently from the publication supplement and reconciled against its phenotype table. These source categories were evaluated only as audit comparators and were never substituted for independent calls from deposited assemblies. For levofloxacin, the targeted alignment caller was independently checked against amino-acid substitutions derived from the Snippy whole-genome alignment. Agreement was calculated among final-QC isolates for which both calls were available.

### Outcomes and statistical analysis

For each drug and cohort, we estimated sensitivity, specificity, false-susceptible and false-resistant rates, balanced accuracy, Matthews correlation coefficient, positive and negative predictive values, and exact 95% binomial intervals. A cohort was considered externally estimable for the frozen classification only when at least 10 susceptible and 10 resistant isolates were callable. Group bootstrap confidence intervals used 2,000 replicates and seed 20260830, with near-clone component as the fallback unit because verified patient identifiers were unavailable. Deterministic binary panels received explicitly labelled binary-score AUROC, AUPRC, and Brier summaries but no pseudo-calibration. Logistic models used predicted probabilities for AUROC, AUPRC, Brier score, and logistic calibration intercept and slope.

Ningxia MIC summaries retained inequality operators and were treated as cohort-limited lower-bound ranks rather than exact uncensored continuous outcomes. Mutation-prediction groups were compared descriptively and with a prespecified Mann–Whitney rank test; this could not substitute for a multi-cohort MIC model. Known laboratory and strain contributions to MIC measurement variation further motivated cohort-specific rather than pooled interpretation [@Mouton2018MICVariation].

### Negative controls and transportability classification

Sixteen prespecified robustness items covered validation design, near-clone thinning, raw-read versus assembly support, breakpoint and borderline-MIC interpretations, assay and genome-quality strata, country and lineage strata, a lineage-only model, 100 phenotype-blind size/prevalence-matched random core-SNP panels, and 100 training-label permutations. One-isolate-per-patient analysis was explicitly not estimable because verified patient identifiers were unavailable. Transportability labels were assigned by frozen sensitivity, specificity, false-susceptible, between-cohort difference, and eligible-lineage gates.

### Post-freeze explanatory and stability analyses

After the primary benchmark and transportability labels were frozen, additional analyses were performed to explain failure modes and quantify stability; none could refit a catalogue, alter a phenotype, or change a frozen label. Target callability was compared with contig count, log10 assembly N50, CheckM2 completeness, and contamination using Mann–Whitney tests, Cliff's delta, and descriptive univariable area under the receiver-operating-characteristic curve. Marker combinations and phenotype-versus-marker prevalence gaps were summarized overall and within fixed lineages.

All amino-acid substitutions recoverable across the full Ningxia *gyrA* coding sequence were screened descriptively against the resistant phenotype using two-sided Fisher exact tests with Benjamini–Hochberg correction. An explicitly exploratory add-only N87Y scenario quantified the maximum correction attributable to the single observed off-panel QRDR substitution. Stability analyses comprised 2,000 near-clone-group bootstraps, leave-one-isolate-out recomputation for Ningxia levofloxacin, a grid spanning minimum external denominators and false-susceptible gates, and positive/negative predictive-value curves across assumed resistance prevalences. The latter were scenario-derived from observed sensitivity and specificity and were not presented as empirical calibration.

To decompose post-freeze transport failure, a prespecified explanatory framework separated analytic availability, genomic population shift, conditional genotype–phenotype transport, and clinical error severity. Five-fold stratified near-clone-grouped logistic discriminators used only the first 10 development-fitted core-SNP components to distinguish HpGP from each external cohort. Out-of-fold AUC uncertainty used 2,000 group-bootstrap replicates, and significance used 1,000 cohort-label permutations. Sensitivity, specificity, false-susceptible rate, and resistance among marker-negative isolates were estimated within every fixed SNP cluster with exact intervals. HpGP sensitivity and specificity were directly standardized to each external cohort's phenotype-specific lineage distribution; this reweighting changed neither catalogue nor external prediction. Dominant-lineage differences used two-sided Fisher exact tests. Finally, Ningxia resistant isolates were summarized across lower-bound MIC thresholds of 2, 4, 8, 16, and 32 mg/L, retaining right-censoring flags.

Coverage-aware stress tests used every phenotype-linked isolate with a binary S/R label as the denominator, including isolates excluded by genome QC or target uncallability. The endpoint was the proportion yielding a correct primary result, not diagnostic accuracy among evaluable isolates. For sensitivity and specificity, logical identification bounds assigned every unresolved resistant or susceptible isolate to the least or most favourable compatible prediction; these are deterministic missing-result bounds rather than confidence intervals. A phenotype-blind selective-reporting analysis accepted isolates below fixed 5th, 10th, 20th, 50th, 75th, 90th, 95th, 99th, and 100th percentiles of the HpGP five-nearest-neighbour distance distribution. No external phenotype was used to select a cutoff. Full-cohort levofloxacin sensitivity, specificity, and false-susceptible-rate differences between the two external cohorts used Newcombe independent-proportion intervals and two-sided Fisher exact tests; the balanced-accuracy difference used the existing 2,000 near-clone-group bootstrap distributions. These post-freeze analyses could not change a primary prediction, safety gate, or transportability label.

## Results

### Cohort linkage, genome quality, and target callability

Exact phenotype-to-sequence linkage produced 414 HpGP assemblies, 60 Ningxia assemblies, and 52 paired-read datasets with support assemblies (526 materialized genomes). After the frozen basic and CheckM2 gates, 517 genomes remained: 414/414 HpGP, 57/60 Ningxia, and 46/52 read-cohort genomes (Figure 1; Table S1). Three Ningxia and six read-cohort support assemblies failed genome-level QC and were excluded before relatedness, lineage, and diagnostic analyses.

Target callability differed materially by sequence product. Both targets were callable in all 414 HpGP assemblies. In Ningxia, *gyrA* was callable in 57/60 phenotype-linked isolates, but 23S rRNA was target-spanning in only 6/60 assemblies (10.0%). The remaining 54 were classified as uncallable, not susceptible. In the read cohort, 23S rRNA was callable in 46/52 isolates (88.5%) and *gyrA* in 42/52 (80.8%); after exclusion of ambiguous phenotypes, the primary S/R denominators were 44 and 39, respectively (Table S2). Within Ningxia, 23S-callable and uncallable assemblies were not distinguished by contig count (P=0.815), log10 N50 (P=0.639), CheckM2 completeness (P=0.199), or contamination (P=0.499), indicating that ordinary whole-assembly summary statistics did not explain repeated-target recovery (Supplementary Figure S1; Table S14). The post-freeze grid yielded six callable final-QC assemblies under every tested task/identity/coverage combination; 53/60 assemblies had only partial 23S-like hits without marker-spanning context, and no final-QC assembly was rescued by threshold relaxation (Supplementary Figure S7; Tables S19a,b).

### Near-clone and lineage gates

Full Mash/skani screening identified four two-isolate near-clone components: FRA-012/FRA-014, GRE-041/GRE-046, POL-106/POL-108, and TUR-002/TUR-005. Every pair was confined to HpGP; no cross-cohort near clone was detected. Near-clone thinning therefore did not remove an external test isolate paired with an HpGP genome (Tables S3a,b).

The core alignment contained 518 records including the reference and 236,415 aligned nucleotides. The phenotype-blind lineage matrix contained 217,003 variable sites. Eight clusters fitted in HpGP contained 128, 2, 156, 110, 10, 65, 19, and 27 genomes after projection of the external cohorts (Figure 2). Ningxia projected mainly to cluster 3 (52/57), with four isolates in cluster 1 and one in cluster 4. The read cohort also projected mainly to cluster 3 (44/46), with two isolates in cluster 1. Cohort lineage compositions consequently diverged from HpGP (Jensen–Shannon distances 0.720 for Ningxia and 0.773 for the read cohort).

Despite this compositional shift, external genomes were not geometrically remote from HpGP in the 10-component development manifold. Median five-nearest-HpGP distances were 0.406 for HpGP, 0.135 for Ningxia, and 0.116 for the read cohort (both external comparisons P<1.1e-18). In Ningxia levofloxacin, incorrect calls were no farther from HpGP than correct calls (median 0.134 versus 0.135; P=0.968; Cliff's delta 0.008). Thus, the failure occurred within a densely represented development-space neighbourhood and was not explained by simple geometric out-of-distribution distance. Lineage-specific external performance remained most informative in cluster 3, but study and lineage were strongly confounded (Tables S15a,b).

### Frozen-panel internal and external performance

In HpGP, the frozen clarithromycin panel correctly classified all 108 resistant and 306 susceptible isolates (sensitivity and specificity 100%). The levofloxacin panel classified 131/133 resistant and 281/281 susceptible isolates (sensitivity 98.5%, 95% CI 94.7–99.8; specificity 100%, 98.7–100), with two false-susceptible predictions.

In the raw-read external cohort, the clarithromycin panel produced 18 true-resistant, 23 true-susceptible, one false-resistant, and two false-susceptible predictions among 44 primary S/R isolates. Sensitivity was 90.0% (95% CI 68.3–98.8), specificity 95.8% (78.9–99.9), false-susceptible rate 10.0%, balanced accuracy 92.9%, and Matthews correlation coefficient 0.863. The levofloxacin panel produced 14 true-resistant, 22 true-susceptible, one false-resistant, and two false-susceptible predictions among 39 isolates. Sensitivity was 87.5% (61.7–98.4), specificity 95.7% (78.1–99.9), false-susceptible rate 12.5%, balanced accuracy 91.6%, and Matthews correlation coefficient 0.841.

Ningxia clarithromycin was not an estimable external validation because only six assemblies were callable, comprising two resistant and four susceptible isolates. Although all six were classified correctly, this selected 10% subset was not treated as evidence of cohort-level performance. Ningxia levofloxacin was estimable in 57 final-QC isolates and produced 12 true-resistant, 22 true-susceptible, seven false-resistant, and 16 false-susceptible predictions. Sensitivity was 42.9% (95% CI 24.5–62.8), specificity 75.9% (56.5–89.7), false-susceptible rate 57.1%, balanced accuracy 59.4%, and Matthews correlation coefficient 0.199 (Figure 3; Tables S4 and S5).

Ningxia clarithromycin is not estimable because only 6/60 phenotype-linked assemblies were target-callable.](../figures/main/Figure3_external_performance_frozen_catalogues.png){#fig-performance width=100%}

### Validation design and lineage-stratified performance

For the mutation-only clarithromycin model, mean balanced accuracy was 1.000 under both random-isolate and clone-grouped internal validation, 0.957 under leave-lineage-out validation, and 0.929 in the estimable external read cohort. For levofloxacin, the corresponding internal balanced accuracies were 0.980, 0.954, and 0.990, whereas the mean across the two external cohorts was 0.755 (standard deviation 0.228): 0.594 in Ningxia and 0.916 in the read cohort (Figure 4; Tables S6a,b). Lineage-only models were close to chance and generally predicted the majority susceptible class.

Across all cohorts, cluster 3 had clarithromycin sensitivity 95.5% and specificity 98.4% among 108 evaluable isolates. For levofloxacin, cluster 3 sensitivity was 78.3%, specificity 91.0%, false-susceptible rate 21.7%, and balanced accuracy 84.7% among 149 isolates. Cluster 1 levofloxacin sensitivity was 90.2% and specificity 100%; cluster 4 sensitivity was 96.6% and specificity 100%. The lower cluster 3 result was consistent with the concentration of external failures in that cluster, but the design could not separate lineage from study, sequence snapshot, or susceptibility-testing effects (Supplementary Figure S4).

### MIC distributions, source-genotype audit, and robustness controls

Among the 57 Ningxia isolates with callable levofloxacin predictions, the marker-resistant group had a median lower-bound MIC of 8 mg/L (19 isolates; seven right-censored) compared with 0.75 mg/L in the marker-susceptible group (38 isolates; six right-censored). The distributions overlapped broadly and the exploratory Mann–Whitney test was not conventionally significant (P=0.0604). The clarithromycin comparison included only six callable isolates and was not informative (P=0.0952; Table S9).

The source-reported Ningxia *gyrA* genotype categories showed levofloxacin sensitivity 89.7% and specificity 93.5% across all 60 source rows; among 57 final-QC genomes, the corresponding values were 89.3% and 93.1%. However, the source-reported category agreed with the independently recalled frozen-panel call in only 31/57 final-QC isolates (54.4%). In contrast, the targeted alignment caller and an independent Snippy whole-genome-alignment caller agreed on all 57 frozen-panel calls. Of 16 independently recalled false-susceptible isolates, one carried an off-panel N87Y substitution and the other 15 were wild type at the frozen QRDR positions in both independent call sets. In the exploratory add-only scenario, N87Y increased sensitivity from 42.9% to 46.4% and reduced the false-susceptible rate from 57.1% to 53.6%, with specificity unchanged at 75.9% (Table S10).

The full-*gyrA* missense screen did not identify a residual variant associated with resistance after Benjamini–Hochberg correction (minimum adjusted P=0.313). This negative scan does not exclude regulatory, structural, heteroresistant, non-*gyrA*, phenotype, or provenance explanations; it shows only that no single recurrent missense substitution recoverable from these assemblies explained the discrepancy (Supplementary Figures S2 and S6; Tables S16a-c).

Raw-read and support-assembly calls agreed whenever both were callable in the read cohort (44/44 clarithromycin and 41/41 levofloxacin). Near-clone thinning did not change external results. Size- and prevalence-matched random SNP panels and training-label permutations produced mean balanced accuracies near 0.50. Phenotype-reinterpretation and genome-quality sensitivity outputs did not convert the main transportability classifications. A one-isolate-per-patient analysis remained not estimable because patient identifiers were unavailable (Figure 5; Supplementary Figure S3; Tables S7a,b and S8a-d).

### Frozen transportability classification

Clarithromycin was classified `INSUFFICIENT_DATA` because fewer than two external cohorts met the frozen requirement of at least 10 susceptible and 10 resistant callable isolates. The read-cohort estimate was encouraging but its 10.0% false-susceptible rate sat at the prespecified boundary, and the Ningxia assembly snapshot could not provide an independent cohort-level estimate. Levofloxacin was classified `HIGH_FALSE_SUSCEPTIBLE_RISK` because Ningxia exceeded the frozen 10% false-susceptible gate, with a point estimate of 57.1% (Figure 6; Table S11). These labels apply to the tested catalogue, public sequence snapshots, and assay-linked cohorts; they are not universal biological properties of the antibiotics or mutations.

(b) Frozen drug-level interpretation. (c, d) Classification over a grid of minimum external denominators and false-susceptible thresholds; squares mark the frozen settings. Grey denotes insufficient data, orange high risk, and green exploratory pass.](../figures/main/Figure6_transportability_boundaries.png){#fig-boundaries width=100%}

### Mutation architecture and phenotype-marker prevalence shifts

Across HpGP, the most frequent clarithromycin resistance marker was A2143G, whereas levofloxacin resistance was distributed across N87 and D91 substitutions (Figure 7). External cohorts showed shifts in individual marker prevalence and lineage composition, but no novel marker combination dominated the Ningxia error set. The marker-resistance prevalence closely tracked phenotypic resistance in HpGP (gap -0.5 percentage points for levofloxacin) and the read cohort (-2.6 points), but underestimated Ningxia levofloxacin resistance by 15.8 points. All 16 Ningxia levofloxacin false-susceptible isolates were marker-wild type under the frozen rule, while six of seven false-resistant isolates carried N87K. The lineage-stratified prevalence map localized much of the discrepancy to cluster 3, but sparse external membership in other clusters prevented separation of study and lineage effects (Tables S13a,b).

![Figure 7. Mutation architecture and phenotype-marker prevalence shifts. (a, b) Cohort-specific carrier prevalence for frozen clarithromycin and levofloxacin markers. (c) Most frequent marker combinations. (d) Phenotypic versus marker-defined resistance prevalence. (e) Lineage-specific levofloxacin marker-minus-phenotype prevalence gaps. (f) Callable-isolate outcome composition. Heatmaps describe observed carriers and do not estimate causal effects.](../figures/main/Figure7_mutation_architecture_prevalence_shift.png){#fig-mutation-architecture width=100%}

### Influence, bootstrap, and prevalence-scenario robustness

The Ningxia levofloxacin result was not driven by one isolate. Across all 57 leave-one-isolate-out analyses, the false-susceptible rate ranged from 55.6% to 59.3% and balanced accuracy from 58.3% to 60.7% (Figure 8). The 2,000 group-bootstrap distributions retained the large contrast between Ningxia and the read cohort, while also showing the uncertainty expected from modest external denominators. Predictive-value curves showed that the clinical meaning of each fixed sensitivity/specificity pair varied with assumed resistance prevalence; critically, the lower Ningxia sensitivity eroded the negative predictive value as prevalence increased. These curves are scenario calculations and do not constitute calibration in a new population (Tables S17a-d).

![Figure 8. Robustness and prevalence-dependent predictive values. (a, b) Ningxia levofloxacin false-susceptible rate and balanced accuracy after dropping each isolate in turn. (c, d) Group-bootstrap distributions of external balanced accuracy and false-susceptible rate. (e, f) Positive and negative predictive values implied by observed sensitivity and specificity over assumed resistance prevalences. Dashed lines mark the frozen false-susceptible boundary or observed cohort prevalence where applicable.](../figures/main/Figure8_robustness_predictive_values.png){#fig-robustness width=100%}

### Four-domain transport shift and clinical severity

The expanded transport audit separated target availability from population and conditional shifts (Figure 9). Although external genomes occupied dense HpGP neighbourhoods, the first 10 phenotype-blind core-SNP components identified study membership with out-of-fold AUC 0.899 (95% group-bootstrap interval 0.871–0.924) for Ningxia versus HpGP and 0.918 (0.893–0.941) for the read cohort versus HpGP; no value from either 1,000-permutation null distribution reached the observed mean fold AUC (P=0.001). Thus, local manifold support and learnable cohort-level covariate shift coexisted (Supplementary Figure S5).

Lineage composition alone did not reproduce the Ningxia performance loss. Direct standardization of HpGP to the Ningxia phenotype-specific lineage distribution yielded 100% expected sensitivity and specificity, compared with observed Ningxia estimates of 42.9% and 75.9%. Within dominant SNP cluster 3, Ningxia sensitivity was 12/23 (52.2%) versus 22/22 (100%) in HpGP (Fisher P=0.00020), while specificity was 22/29 (75.9%) versus 38/38 (100%; P=0.0018). Among frozen-marker-negative cluster-3 isolates, resistance occurred in 11/33 Ningxia isolates, 0/38 HpGP isolates (P=0.000076), and 2/23 read-cohort isolates. This is evidence of study-conditioned association within the shared computational cluster, not proof of a causal lineage mechanism.

The missed resistance was clinically substantial rather than confined to the breakpoint margin. The 16 false-susceptible Ningxia isolates had a median lower-bound MIC of 16 mg/L (interquartile range 3.5–32); 11/16 had MIC at least 8 mg/L and six were right-censored above 32 mg/L. These severity summaries, together with the stable leave-one-isolate-out result, place the levofloxacin failure at the conditional-transport and clinical-consequence layers rather than at callability alone (Tables S18a-d).

(a) Data-supported framework spanning analytic availability, genomic population shift, conditional genotype–phenotype transport, and clinical consequence. (b) Out-of-fold AUCs from phenotype-blind PC-only cohort discriminators with group-bootstrap intervals. (c) Dominant SNP-cluster-3 sensitivity and specificity with exact intervals. (d) Resistance among frozen-marker-negative cluster-3 isolates. (e) Observed Ningxia performance compared with crude HpGP and HpGP standardized to the Ningxia phenotype-specific lineage distribution. (f) Proportion of detected and missed resistant Ningxia isolates at or above increasing lower-bound MIC thresholds. Post-freeze analyses explain but do not refit the frozen catalogue.](../figures/main/Figure9_three_layer_transport_shift.png){#fig-transport-shift width=100%}

### Coverage-aware yield, partial-identification bounds, and selective reporting

When every phenotype-linked binary isolate was retained in the denominator, 6/60 Ningxia isolates (10.0%) yielded a correct clarithromycin result and 34/60 (56.7%) yielded a correct levofloxacin result. The corresponding read-cohort yields were 41/50 (82.0%) and 36/48 (75.0%). Because 29/31 resistant and 25/29 susceptible Ningxia clarithromycin isolates were unresolved, the apparently perfect six-isolate callable subset was compatible with full-cohort sensitivity anywhere from 6.5% to 100% and specificity from 13.8% to 100%. These logical bounds formally show why the callable subset cannot identify diagnostic performance (Supplementary Figure S8a-c; Table S20a,b).

Phenotype-blind abstention based on development-manifold distance did not provide a safe transport filter. Across the fixed HpGP percentile cutoffs, every eligible Ningxia levofloxacin subset failed the frozen safety gate; the lowest false-susceptible rate was 50.0% while retaining 50/57 primary isolates (87.7% coverage). By contrast, read-cohort false-susceptible rates remained 12.5-16.7% across the evaluated cutoffs, but still did not satisfy the 10% gate. Thus, rejecting geometrically less familiar genomes could not isolate a reliable Ningxia subset (Supplementary Figure S8e,f; Table S20c).

The two external levofloxacin settings were formally heterogeneous. Ningxia sensitivity was 44.6 percentage points lower than in the read cohort (95% Newcombe interval -63.3 to -15.0; Fisher P=0.0046), while specificity was 19.8 points lower (-38.1 to 0.7; P=0.0635). The false-susceptible-rate difference was consequently +44.6 points (15.0 to 63.3), and the balanced-accuracy difference was -32.2 points (95% group-bootstrap interval -47.1 to -17.4). These contrasts support cohort-specific reporting rather than a pooled external estimate (Supplementary Figure S8d; Table S20d).

## Discussion

This audit-first benchmark found a marked separation between catalogue/internal accuracy and performance in one external public sequence snapshot. The fixed 23S rRNA catalogue performed well in the estimable read-based cohort, but clarithromycin transportability could not be declared because 90% of the Ningxia assemblies lacked a target-spanning 23S call. The fixed *gyrA* catalogue also performed well in the read cohort but failed the prespecified false-susceptible safety gate in Ningxia. These results do not support a single pooled cross-cohort accuracy claim.

The validation-design analysis argues against conventional near-clone leakage as the principal explanation. Only four near-clone pairs were identified, all within HpGP; no near clone bridged a development and external cohort. Clone-grouped and leave-lineage-out internal estimates remained high, while external Ningxia performance fell sharply. External cohorts had markedly shifted lineage compositions, yet their genomes were near densely represented HpGP neighbourhoods and Ningxia errors were no farther from HpGP than correct calls. The adversarial analysis resolves this apparent tension: local support did not imply cohort exchangeability, because phenotype-blind PCs still distinguished each external study from HpGP with AUC near 0.90. More importantly, direct lineage standardization retained 100% expected HpGP sensitivity and specificity, while the gap persisted within cluster 3. The discontinuity therefore occurred at the study-conditioned genotype–phenotype and provenance boundary, rather than being explained by random versus clone-aware splitting, simple geometric remoteness, or marginal lineage composition alone. Because study, assay, sequence snapshot, and cluster membership remain partially confounded, these results do not identify a causal lineage mechanism.

Clarithromycin illustrates why callability is a diagnostic outcome. Treating absence of a target-spanning 23S sequence as wild type would have converted technical missingness into apparent susceptibility and could have produced a dangerously inflated denominator. The six callable Ningxia assemblies happened to be classified correctly, but they represented only 10% of the phenotype-linked cohort and were not representative evidence. Their general contiguity and CheckM2 summaries did not differ detectably from the 54 uncallable assemblies. More decisively, neither a sensitive BLAST task nor broad identity/coverage relaxation rescued another final-QC target-spanning assembly. When unresolved resistant and susceptible isolates were retained rather than dropped, the logical sensitivity and specificity ranges widened to 6.5-100% and 13.8-100%, and only 10% of phenotype-linked isolates yielded a correct result. The bottleneck was therefore marker-spanning assembly context rather than an arbitrarily strict similarity threshold. In contrast, direct read mapping made 23S callable in most isolates in the second external cohort. Repeated resistance loci therefore require sequence-product-specific validation, explicit uncallable reporting, and a denominator that reflects end-to-end result yield.

The Ningxia levofloxacin discrepancy was not resolved by re-running a second independent caller. Targeted alignment and whole-genome-alignment calls agreed in all 57 final-QC assemblies, yet the independent call agreed with the source-reported genotype category in only 54.4%. The source-reported categories retained much stronger phenotype performance than the independently recalled deposited-assembly calls. Possible explanations include a difference between the sequence snapshot used for the source analysis and the currently deposited assemblies, isolate-to-phenotype linkage provenance, within-isolate heterogeneity or evolution, or differences in the source genotyping pipeline. The available public files do not distinguish among these possibilities, and the discrepancy should not be interpreted as evidence of error by the source investigators. It does demonstrate that publication-level genotype performance cannot be substituted for independent sequence recall and that validated AMR resources require versioned sequence–phenotype provenance [@Feldgarden2019AMRFinder].

Catalogue incompleteness explained only a small part of the levofloxacin false-susceptible burden. N87Y, included in the source rule but excluded from the frozen HpGP panel, appeared in one of 16 Ningxia false-susceptible isolates. Adding it post hoc recovered only that isolate, and no other full-*gyrA* missense variant survived false-discovery correction. The other 15 false-susceptible isolates were wild type at the frozen QRDR positions under both callers. Expanding the catalogue after inspecting the test cohort would violate the analysis lock and, in this case, could not recover most failures. Non-catalogued mechanisms, phenotype measurement, linkage, and sequence-provenance differences remain alternative explanations requiring new data rather than post hoc marker selection.

The clinical direction of error matters. A false-resistant call may lead clinicians away from an active drug, but a false-susceptible call risks recommending an ineffective regimen. The 57.1% false-susceptible rate for levofloxacin in Ningxia was therefore the decisive frozen safety result, even though the read cohort performed substantially better. It remained above 55% after removal of any single isolate, and the high-risk or insufficient-data interpretations persisted over broad threshold and denominator grids. The missed isolates were not simply close to the breakpoint: their median lower-bound MIC was 16 mg/L, 11/16 were at least 8 mg/L, and six were right-censored above 32 mg/L. The formal external sensitivity difference of -44.6 percentage points and balanced-accuracy difference of -32.2 points quantify this heterogeneity. Moreover, phenotype-blind rejection of less familiar genomes could not lower the Ningxia false-susceptible rate below 50%, showing that simple geometric abstention is not a sufficient transport safeguard. The observed heterogeneity cautions against averaging across studies with different sequence products and phenotype procedures. Prevalence-scenario curves further show why transportability cannot be summarized by one context-free predictive value.

This study has several strengths. Cohort eligibility required exact isolate-level phenotype-to-sequence linkage; marker panels, denominators, and safety gates were frozen before complete performance inspection; missing targets remained uncallable; population structure was fitted without external phenotypes; and source-genotype findings were kept separate from independently recalled predictions. Raw-read versus support-assembly agreement, independent caller concordance, random-marker controls, label permutations, near-clone-aware analyses, continuous manifold proximity, adversarial cohort discrimination, lineage standardization, within-lineage conditional estimates, full-gene residual screening, MIC-severity profiling, end-to-end yield accounting, partial-identification bounds, phenotype-blind abstention, external-cohort difference intervals, group bootstrap, and leave-one-out influence analysis provided orthogonal technical checks.

The limitations are equally important. Both external cohorts were Chinese, so the study does not establish global geographic transportability. Cohorts were small, and confidence intervals were wide. Original Ningxia reads were not publicly linked, making 23S largely uncallable and preventing reconstruction of the exact source sequence snapshot or mixed alleles. The read cohort used study-defined disk labels with overlapping levofloxacin threshold descriptions rather than MICs. Verified patient identifiers were unavailable, precluding one-isolate-per-patient analysis. HpGP was an internal/catalogue benchmark rather than an independent clinical validation cohort. The computational clusters were not formal named populations, and geometric proximity cannot establish exchangeability. The logical callability bounds are worst/best-case identification ranges rather than sampling intervals, and the abstention thresholds are diagnostic stress tests rather than a validated deployment rule. The full-*gyrA* scan, N87Y rescue, 23S threshold grid, coverage-aware bounds, and selective-reporting analysis were post-freeze explanatory analyses and require independent replication. No wet-laboratory reculture, repeat AST, targeted sequencing, or causal mechanism experiment was available.

In conclusion, the fixed clarithromycin catalogue had encouraging external read-cohort performance but insufficient cross-cohort evidence, while the fixed levofloxacin catalogue showed high false-susceptible risk in one external assembly cohort. The expanded analysis shows that transportability is a chain: target availability, cohort-level genomic shift, conditional genotype–phenotype stability, and error severity must all be evaluated. Before clinical use, resistance-genotyping studies should validate version-matched raw sequence data, publish exact isolate–phenotype–sequence crosswalks, report target uncallability as an outcome, and reproduce calls independently across studies and lineages.
